name: comparisonForm_mem_integralForms
summary: Termwise: the delta forms do not increase the gauge, the Cartan product loses at most |g|_p^{−loss}, which g^loss repays, and the line multipliers and the table vectors are integral.

steps.claim: Expand gl ζ as a sum of class sums of product forms; integral forms are closed under sums, so it suffices to treat one term.
steps.lean:
simp_rw [comparisonForm_apply, classSum, finsum_eq_sum_of_fintype, smul_sum]
  refine sum_mem fun b _ ↦ sum_mem fun _ _ _ ↦ ?_

steps.claim: The level of the class sum is free (classAut_rowFixingLevel_eq_bot).

The gauge of the term is at most |g|^{loss}·(gauge of the delta form) ≤ |g|^{loss}·|g|^{−loss}·(gauge of the line multiplier)·(gauge of conj ζ) ≤ 1: weylGauge_smul, weylGauge_deltaForm_le (finite-order level character), weylGauge_cartanProduct_le with M = g (g lies in the ideal of the chosen places), the integrality of the line multipliers (lineScale, p prime to N(Q)), and hζ.
steps.lean:
grw (transparency := default) [weylGauge_smul, weylGauge_deltaForm_le isOfFinOrder_level_char,
    weylGauge_mul, (splittingV j ϑ).weylGauge_cartanProduct_le (M := D.gProd)
    (D.ideal_untwistedModulus_eq_span.ge (by simp [← piGBar_mul_star, Ideal.mul_mem_right]))
    (glueLattice ..).2, ((lineScale j).2.2
    ..).1 _ q, hζ] <;> simp [Kf_le_localLevel _, mul_inv_le_one]; simp [weylGauge]
